1003565.etyen:
Inherited from Old Norse jórtr (“rumination”), related to jórtra (“to ruminate”), whence jorte (“to ruminate, chew the cud”), and to ørt (“rumination; cud”).
The wider Germanic word family has been analysed as containing an iterative element meaning “again, repeatedly” and a verbal base ultimately related to *h₁rewg- (“to belch, roar”).
